title: Systems with Infinitely Many Solutions Review Test
description: Practice and explain systems with infinitely many solutions.

questions.questionText: The equations y = 11x + 2 and 2y = 22x + 4 describe which graphs?
questions.explanation: Dividing the second equation by 2 gives the first equation, so every point on the line is shared.

questions.questionText: Subtracting equivalent equations 11x + y = 8 and 11x + y = 8 gives 0 = 0. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: The identity shows that the two equations impose the same condition, not that both coordinates must be zero.

questions.questionText: Complete a copy of x + y = 16: 3x + 3y = __.
questions.explanation: Multiplying an equation by 3 requires multiplying both sides, including the constant, by 3.

questions.questionText: Both equations of a system reduce to y = x + 11. Must (0, 0) solve the system?
questions.correctAnswer: No; the line does not pass through (0, 0).
questions.explanation: At x = 0 the shared line has y = 11, not zero. Infinite solutions are restricted to the shared line.
options: Yes; infinitely many solutions includes every point.
Yes; all lines pass through the origin.
No; the line does not pass through (0, 0).
No; the system has no solutions.

questions.questionText: A system has two copies of y = 11x. Which describes its solution set?
questions.explanation: Choose any real x-value t; y must still equal the slope times t.

questions.questionText: The equations y = 12x + 2 and 2y = 24x + 4 describe which graphs?
questions.explanation: Dividing the second equation by 2 gives the first equation, so every point on the line is shared.

questions.questionText: Subtracting equivalent equations 12x + y = 8 and 12x + y = 8 gives 0 = 0. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: The identity shows that the two equations impose the same condition, not that both coordinates must be zero.

questions.questionText: Complete a copy of x + y = 17: 3x + 3y = __.
questions.explanation: Multiplying an equation by 3 requires multiplying both sides, including the constant, by 3.

questions.questionText: For infinitely many solutions, what must k be in 2x + 3y = 17 and 6x + 9y = k?
questions.explanation: The coefficients are tripled, so the right side must be tripled too.

questions.questionText: Compare 2y = 22x + 6 with y = 11x + 4. Why are there not infinitely many solutions?
questions.correctAnswer: Their slopes match but their intercepts differ.
questions.explanation: The first equation is y = 11x + 3; the second has intercept 4. They are distinct parallel lines.
options: Their slopes match but their intercepts differ.
Multiplying by 2 changes the solution set.
The two equations describe the same line.

questions.questionText: The system is x + y = 21 and 4x + 4y = 84. Which listed pair is a solution?
questions.explanation: The pair sums to 21; multiplying that sum by 4 satisfies the second equation as well.

questions.questionText: A student doubles x + 11y = 7 and writes 2x + 22y = 7. What is the error?
questions.correctAnswer: The constant must also be doubled to 14.
questions.explanation: Equivalent equations require applying the nonzero multiplier to every term on both sides.
options: The constant must also be doubled to 14.

questions.questionText: A system has infinitely many solutions: y = 2x + 11 and y = ax + 11. Find a.
questions.explanation: Both slope and intercept must match. The shared intercept is already correct; the slope must be 2.

questions.questionText: For infinitely many solutions, what must k be in 2x + 3y = 18 and 6x + 9y = k?
questions.explanation: The coefficients are tripled, so the right side must be tripled too.

Their slopes match but their intercepts differ.
